tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.
tools.name: wait

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` selects an existing tab. `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

On Windows, choose the requested window by app and title from the inventory. Pass the selected window's ID as returned.

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp({ windowId: selected.id });
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images, videos, and audio using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When an app or connector generates or edits media, prefer native media already displayed inline or a local output file already returned by the tool. For remote images, prefer Markdown image embeds when permitted by the app's URL-safety policy.
- When presenting media that cannot be displayed directly, including remote video and audio, use the app's preview or display tool when available. Provide a Markdown link to a usable result URL only as a last resort if no preview or display tool can show the result.
- Do not download remote media to bypass the app's restrictions on presenting it to the user.
- When sending or referencing a local image, video, or audio file, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the media.
- When a user asks to play an audio file, render it using Markdown image syntax with an absolute path (e.g., ![audio](/absolute/path.mp3)).
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Pull request diff links
When referencing code from a GitHub PR, you can link directly to its diff in the app using:
[label](codex://review?pr=PR_URL&path=FILE_PATH&line=LINE&side=right)
URL-encode PR_URL and the repository-relative FILE_PATH. Use a verified one-based LINE from the current PR diff. Use side=left for the original code or side=right for the updated code. Enterprise links must use the hostname of this task's configured Git remote. Use ordinary file links for workspace code.

### Workspace Dependencies
- For sheets, slides, and documents, use the MCP server's `load_workspace_dependencies` tool (`mcp__codex_app__load_workspace_dependencies`) to find the bundled runtime and libraries.

### Automations
- When you write or rewrite an automation prompt, keep it within 10,000 estimated tokens.
- When the user asks to manage an app automation, set a reminder, or schedule a recurring task, use the relevant Automations action to help the user. Do not write raw automation directives by hand.
- Create an automation when the user wants a reminder, a recurring report, or a standing alert for future events.
- Do not create an automation to track a specific job or task through a milestone, failure, or completion. If the user asks you to watch a run or task to completion, keep checking in the current task and follow through when the requested condition is met.
- Unless the user asks for periodic updates, notify them only on a meaningful change, completion, failure, or required user action.
- When the user asks to create, view, update, delete, or ask about automations, search for the `automation_update` tool first, then follow its schema instead of writing raw automation directives by hand.
- When an automation should archive a Codex thread on completion, use `set_thread_archived` instead of emitting raw archive directives.

### Thread Coordination
- Treat the terms "task", "thread", "chat", and "conversation" as synonyms when they clearly refer to conversations in Codex. Use "chat" when referring to conversations in the product. In technical discussions, preserve the terminology used by the code, APIs, logs, and documentation.
- When the user asks to create, fork, inspect, continue, hand off, pin, archive, unarchive, permanently delete, rename, or otherwise manage Codex threads, search for the relevant thread tool first: `create_thread`, `fork_thread`, `list_threads`, `list_archived_threads`, `read_thread`, `wait_threads`, `send_message_to_thread`, `handoff_thread`, `set_thread_pinned`, `set_thread_archived`, `delete_thread`, or `set_thread_title`.
- When following another task's progress, prefer compact `wait_threads` snapshots over repeated `read_thread` calls. Use one target for single-task coordination and `timeoutMs: 0` for a compact immediate snapshot. `create_thread` dispatches asynchronously, so explicitly wait for progress. Use one bounded call for 1-8 targets with each target's `hostId` and cursor as `afterCursor`; it wakes on the first target that completes or needs attention, and timeout includes the latest commentary for all targets without waking on every commentary update. An up-to-date cursor suppresses already-delivered final text. Separate waits from one task may run serially. Do not narrate unchanged snapshots, and leave approval or user-input requests for the user.
- Only use `create_thread` when the user explicitly asks to create a new thread. Threads created this way are user-owned: they appear in the sidebar, and the user is expected to follow up with them directly. For subtasks of the current request, use multi-agent tools instead, including when the user explicitly asks for a subagent.
- After a successful `create_thread` call, emit `::created-thread{threadId="..."}` for a created thread or `::created-thread{clientThreadId="..."}` for queued worktree setup on its own line in your final response.

### Inline Code Comments
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive when you need to attach feedback directly to specific code lines.
- Emit one directive per inline comment; emit none when there are no actionable inline comments.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3).
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix by default when creating branches, but follow the user's request if they want a different prefix.
</app-context>

1. Persistent Router：一个长期存在的主 Session，负责所有用户交互、全局记忆和任务协调。

6. Chain of Recall：通过对象引用关系恢复历史任务、项目状态、决策和执行记录。
7. Persistent State：Conversation、Router、Worker、Quest 和 Event 均可持久化与恢复。
8. Watchdog：监控 Router、Worker、Dispatcher 和执行环境，处理异常退出、超时及恢复。

# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-16

The backend architecture is being corrected around DeepSeek Super-agent's
persistent Router and independent Workers. The default Core delegates ordinary
conversational tasks automatically, filters environmental events, sends Thread
continuations directly to subscribed Workers, follows typed Chain of Recall
references, and supervises durable execution. Plans, Quests and approval records
are internal infrastructure. The frontend is unchanged in this correction.

Read the [architecture audit and refactor plan](docs/SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[product architecture](docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[implementation and validation report](docs/SUPERAGENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md)
for the exact implemented behavior, tests, real Provider observations and limits.
Historical Phase 2 evidence remains available below; it does not describe the
new autonomous dispatch path.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` | Operator-supplied Router context ceiling, required when setting a Router model. Core startup requires an integer greater than `2048` and greater than the configured output reserve. |

The Phase 2 live acceptance harness uses a 120-second timeout, a 150-second Worker lease and zero additional
Gateway retries, with a Router output reserve of `4096` and `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS=3`
within the scenario's three-round cap. Router/Planner schema repair remains a separately bounded stage;
neither setting authorizes replay of an unresolved external action.

The current WorkBuddy acceptance harness explicitly requests `reasoning_effort=none`,
which the local proxy implementation advertises for the requested model. This is
an operator setting, not independent proof of the upstream model's internal behavior.
Earlier diagnostic runs used the proxy default and retain their separate results.

The Router reads a bounded snapshot and calls the provider outside the database write
transaction. A successful decision and its messages commit together; provider errors, invalid
decisions, or budget failures leave no messages or Quest changes for that turn. The caller can
retry with the same request ID. The context budget uses a conservative UTF-8 byte estimate,
reserves output and request overhead, and also respects a known registry context window. Tool
access is limited to read-only Core queries. Worker execution separately requires approved plan/team contracts and governed tool permissions.

### Core authentication and development bootstrap

Core requires a fresh cryptographically random 32-byte process secret; `.env` is explicitly rejected. For manual browser development, supply it as 64 hex characters in `FORGE_CORE_SECRET` using a protected input method and enter the same secret into the UI's password field. Never place it in command history, source files, URLs, logs, or persistent browser storage. In the native desktop integration, the parent supplies the secret through a private pipe and the UI receives the derived session bearer in memory. Restarting Core invalidates old bearer tokens. Native integration is still undergoing final verification.

The unauthenticated public loopback `/health` returns only liveness and a random per-process session challenge; an authenticated request also receives Router identity and background status. A trusted client computes the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 over the UTF-8 challenge using the decoded 32-byte secret, and sends `Authorization: Bearer <digest>` on API requests. Requests without an Origin are allowed only with authentication and a loopback peer and Host; browser requests must also use an explicitly allowed Origin. These boundaries protect against unauthorized webpages and other untrusted clients; they do not protect secrets from an attacker who can read the same OS user's process memory. Keep the development server and any allowed origin trusted.

The authenticated user API supports `POST /api/approvals`, `GET /api/approvals?quest_id=...`, `GET /api/approvals/{id}`, and POSTs to `/{id}/decision` or `/{id}/revoke`. Workspace grants use `GET`/`POST /api/quests/{id}/grants` and `POST /api/quests/{id}/grants/revoke`. Decisions and grants record the authenticated local user, not a caller-supplied actor. The bearer represents that user; it must never be exposed to a model or registered as an Agent tool. These routes do not execute actions or accept trusted evidence. The M7 desktop approval and scope controls are under integration testing.

### Workspace and Settings

`python -m forge_api` is the shared Core launcher. From the repository root on Windows, `./scripts/run-backend.ps1` sets up the virtual environment and uses that launcher without shell activation. Pass `-WorkspaceRoot 'D:\YourWorkspace'` to the script, or `python -m forge_api --workspace-root 'D:\YourWorkspace'` directly. Workspace roots must be absolute paths.

The CLI launcher supervises a separate Core process and restarts unexpected exits
with bounded backoff (at most five restarts in ten minutes; five minutes of stable
operation resets that count). Normal shutdown, invalid configuration and a restore
fence stop recovery. A separate supervisor lock prevents duplicate launchers, and
the Core retains its existing Workspace lock. The bootstrap secret reaches the
child through a private pipe; each replacement rotates its session challenge and
invalidates old bearer tokens. On Windows a Job Object drains the Core's descendant
processes before recovery and kills them if the supervisor dies. The native
`--desktop-host` protocol is unchanged; automatic native desktop process restart
is not yet integrated.

The default Workspace is independent of the checkout, installation and shell directory:

| OS | Default Workspace root |
| --- | --- |
| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/FORGE/workspaces/default` |
| Linux | `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/forge/workspaces/default` |

The database defaults to `<WorkspaceRoot>/data/forge.sqlite3`. Settings are loaded as follows:

1. Choose the root using `--workspace-root`, then the process variable `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ROOT`, then the OS default (in that order). A root in `.env` is rejected because the root determines which file to read.
2. Load `<WorkspaceRoot>/.env` if present. `FORGE_ENV_FILE` in the process environment can select another file; relative file names resolve from the root. An explicitly selected missing file is an error. The shell directory's `.env` is ignored. Copy `backend/.env.example` to the selected Workspace root.
3. Process variables override file values. Supported settings are `FORGE_WORKSPACE_ID`, `FORGE_DB_PATH`, `FORGE_HOST` and `FORGE_PORT`; empty values and invalid ports fail startup. `.env` does not expand variables or modify the process environment.
4. Resolve relative database paths from the root and normalize them to absolute paths. The default Workspace ID is a hash of the normalized root; an explicit stable ID supports moving a Workspace. A database already bound to another ID is rejected.

The CLI and desktop Core bootstrap use the same Workspace settings and a new process secret. Direct `uvicorn forge_api.main:app` requires the same secret and loopback binding; prefer the shared launcher.

After a workspace restore, a restore fence blocks writes until an offline review succeeds. Close the desktop and Core, inspect the restored workspace and rollback directory, then use the packaged Python executable with the exact manifest hash and rollback directory shown by the application (replace every placeholder):

```powershell
& 'C:\path\to\packaged\python.exe' -I -m forge_api.maintenance review-restore --workspace-root 'C:\path\to\workspace' --manifest-sha256 '<64-lowercase-hex>' --rollback-directory '.forge-previous-<32-hex>' --reason '<10+ character review reason>'
```

The review validates the source hash, rollback directory name, reason, historical receipts and budget state; unresolved effects or reservations cause it to fail closed. Acknowledging an unknown native operation is a separate action and does not clear the restore fence or establish that the operation succeeded.

Legacy databases are **not discovered or moved automatically**. If an earlier version used `backend/data/forge.sqlite3` or another CWD-relative location, stop its Core process, back up the database with SQLite's backup API (or copy the database and WAL files together while stopped), and set `FORGE_DB_PATH` to its absolute path. Migration failure rolls back the entire pending chain; unknown future versions and ambiguous version metadata are rejected. Downgrades are unsupported.

Events and pending Outbox rows commit in the same transaction as their associated business changes. Durable per-consumer delivery uses leases, fencing, bounded retries, Inbox deduplication and dead-letter/replay records. Historical events migrate as pending. # FORGE Super-agent backend correction

Date: 2026-11-16. Base: `4b220d8bdbd834bbadda53d0baa7756e9c1bb90f`.
The frontend is unchanged. Research preceded implementation; see the
[architecture difference audit and plan](SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[DeepSeek source research](SUPERAGENT_DEEPSEEK_RESEARCH.md) and
[Harness audit](SUPERAGENT_HARNESS_AUDIT.md).

## Resulting architecture

The normal Core entry point uses the persistent Router as the sole conversational
Agent. A request needing execution receives a source-bound host mandate. Internal
execution contracts reuse the existing graph, team and Registry implementation;
routine task admission does not require a human plan/team approval. The mandate
has its own `router_mandate:<id>` actor and cannot impersonate `local_user`.

| Requirement | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Persistent Router | Existing stable `main` conversation/Router identity, bounded context and CAS; autonomous delegation in the real Core lifecycle; user/event Router inference serialized |
| Isolated Workers | Private messages, run identity, leases, per-run working/temp/output paths; fixed process tools use private cwd and temporary environment; Workers report through Router |
| Event-driven triggers | Durable Source/Thread/Trigger ingress, actor/source Fast Path, semantic batched Slow Path; user messages, existing results, authenticated external ingress, persistent timers and file watches |
| Subscription/pass-through | Many-to-many Thread subscriptions, direct Inbox delivery, ingress dedupe, explicit handback and bounded backpressure reconciliation |
| Inline/Spill | Complete original requests and Trigger payloads retained externally; bounded inline content/previews, exact hashes, paginated source reads |
| Chain of Recall | Scoped typed references between conversations, sources, projects, tasks, Workers, runs, plans, events, evidence, memories, receipts and archives |
| Persistent state | Schema 14 migration within the existing strict migration/rollback mechanism; new state shares SQLite transactions and Outbox/CAS boundaries |
| Watchdog | Durable health, bounded loop recovery, expired-lease reconciliation, environment checks and replay-safe Worker recovery; default CLI parent supervisor with process-tree cleanup |
| Generic workspaces | Manifest/Git/plain-directory detection, persistent project/task association and automatic identification from explicit paths in the immutable request |
| Adaptive composition | Router chooses bounded independent assignments/roles; existing Composer chooses eligible models using capability provenance, context/output limits, speed and cost |
| Local tools | Governed file tools, fixed Python/Git probes and read-only GPU diagnostics; existing separately authorized HTTPS browser/MCP tools retained with their original limits |

No duplicate model manager, new frontend, or external agent execution backend was
introduced. Complex execution planning belongs inside Workers. Autonomous
assignments are coarse, independent contracts with no DAG edges.

## Authority and delivery boundaries

An internal mandate permits bounded task scheduling and task-local artifact
writes. It grants no external-action approval. Explicit revocations stay revoked;
crash recovery does not silently recreate them. Each execution still passes
existing plan/team authority, workspace scope, action intent/receipt, model-call
ledger and completion evidence checks.

Core context reads have their own trusted, source-bound checkpoint proofs. They
are not fabricated action receipts. Review verifies run/Quest/plan/call identity,
arguments, result hashes, transcripts, actual Trigger delivery and source scope.
Handback commits once at the checkpoint; subsequent review is read-only. A new
Inbox event arriving during final inference prevents result publication until
the Worker has consumed the continuation. Accounting for the draft remains
charged, and step/tool budgets are not reset.

Watchdog recovery never replays an unknown Provider call or tool effect. Exited
loops use bounded backoff and regain restart allowance only after observed
stable operation. Heartbeat storage failures cannot terminate the recovery loop.
On Windows, the CLI supervisor drains the old Job Object process tree before
starting a replacement. Native desktop bootstrap remains compatible.

The Watchdog reports stale heartbeats but does not cancel or duplicate a pending
loop solely because it is stale. The parent supervises process exit, not a live
Core whose event loop is completely hung. This is infrastructure recovery, not
an independent model Session that judges semantic progress or goal drift.

The cold-start diagnostic, `20261115T190431Z-cold-1f2fe2`, completed two independent

Original reports are preserved; no failed or uncertain call is replayed.

Final responsiveness corrections keep new independent task admission stable
while unrelated Workers change runtime status. Conversation state, messages,
models, constraints, archive head, original task identities, selected recall and
consulted source checks remain fenced; existing-task intents retain the strict
snapshot check. Autonomous routine progress and nonterminal internal status facts

## Operating limits

- Private Worker directories are not an OS sandbox. Process isolation and tool
  authorization do not isolate an attacker with the same OS account.
- Automatic delegation currently uses a fixed local tool allowlist. Terminal
  inspection is a fixed Python-version probe; Python compilation and pure-function
  AST tests do not provide arbitrary shell, pytest, package installation or
  unrestricted program execution. Git support here is status inspection.
- The retained browser tool is allowlisted HTTPS GET, without rendering or
  interactive browsing. MCP is preconfigured HTTPS JSON-RPC `tools/call`, without
  general stdio/SSE discovery or session management. Both retain independent
  high-risk action authorization and are outside the autonomous default allowlist.
  The final live scenarios exercise file tools, not browser or MCP execution.
- Project discovery establishes identity and Recall continuity. It does not
  expand execution outside the configured workspace or grant project writes.
  Multiple explicit roots retain the neutral storage association.
- Autonomous dispatch allows at most four independent assignments; actual
  concurrency also respects the configured Core and Provider limits.
  Workers plan steps inside their own model loop; autonomous nested-team spawning
  is not implemented. Real acceptance uses one configured model for multiple
  roles and operator-supplied capability priors, not a capability benchmark or
  evidence of optimal selection across different models.
- Host contract allocation bounds are enforced. Cumulative token use is recorded,
  with stopping controlled by `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` (default `false`).
  The acceptance drivers explicitly enable their fixed cumulative budgets.
- Timers and file watches are registered by authenticated local host APIs and
  polled by Core. Natural-language creation of schedules/watches is not exposed
  as a Router/Worker tool. External ingress trusts the authenticated local adapter;
  no public webhook server, OAuth/signature adapters or built-in messaging
  connectors are added.
- Automatic whole-Core process restart applies to the default CLI launcher.
  Native `--desktop-host` and direct uvicorn execution do not gain that parent
  supervisor. A running but fully hung process is not automatically restarted.
- Complete Trigger ingress is bounded to 4 MiB; watched files to 1 MiB. Readback
  pages and Recall traversal are bounded, with explicit continuation references.
- GPU support is read-only status through fixed `nvidia-smi` arguments. GPU
  compute scheduling and OS/container security sandboxes are not implemented.
- Tool network access retains operator allowlists and independent action
  authorization. Scheduling a task cannot authorize an external side effect.
- Bounded real scenarios establish observed integration behavior. They do not
  establish arbitrary-task success, indefinite unattended operation or a
  packaged desktop release. The fourteen reproduced historical test failures
  remain visible technical debt.

## Architecture decision

FORGE builds its own general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent. Its product is
one continuous Router conversation with independently executing hidden Workers.
Quest, DAG, team contracts, approvals and evidence are internal infrastructure.
The Router dispatches independent tasks; it does not do detailed task execution.
An execution Worker may use a team internally. Codex and Claude Code inform the
execution harness, context and permissions, rather than the overall architecture.

Primary basis: [DeepSeek Harness article](https://x.com/DeepSeekHarness/status/2116857257245987236),
especially sections 2, 3, 5 and 6, and [official prototype](https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)
at `8c32a9dc5d72c033816c6a8110b37f40cf94fba4`.
The article describes more than the public, single-repository DSH plugin implements.
FORGE adopts the two-layer principles, not its GitHub-only deployment or DSH backend.

## Completed differential audit

Detailed source evidence is in [DeepSeek research](SUPERAGENT_DEEPSEEK_RESEARCH.md),
[harness audit](SUPERAGENT_HARNESS_AUDIT.md) and
[validation baseline](SUPERAGENT_VALIDATION_BASELINE.md).

| Concern | Existing foundation | Gap and minimum correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent Router | Stable `main`, Router ID, durable turns, snapshot/CAS, compaction | Add autonomous delegation to the actual Core lifecycle; keep the Router lightweight |
| Isolated Workers | Hidden session, per-run messages, leases and budgets | Add private per-task execution directories; keep approved input and receipt checks |
| Event triggers | Transactional events/Outbox, Inbox, fenced delivery, retries/dead letters | Durable source/Thread/Trigger intake with code admission and semantic cold-start decisions |
| Subscription/pass-through | Worker commands target one Worker | Many-to-many Thread subscriptions, direct follow-up delivery and explicit handback |
| Inline/Spill | Full message archives, exact hashes and bounded source reads | Apply bounded previews plus complete external content references to triggers/recall |
| Chain of Recall | Sourced lexical/semantic recall, archive links | Typed, bounded traversal across Thread, Trigger, Quest, Worker, event, source and project references |
| Persistent state | SQLite migrations and atomic state/event commits | Persist new trigger/subscription/mandate/watchdog state; use existing contracts and recovery |
| Watchdog | Background exception retry and Worker lease recovery | Independent supervision task, persisted health, timeout/task-exit detection, safe recovery |
| Workspaces | One authoritative workspace binding, optional labels | Generic local manifest/directory discovery and task association, independent of GitHub |
| Model intelligence/teams | Capability provenance, speed/cost, bounded composition | Reuse selection for autonomous independent task assignments rather than ask users to pick Agents |

The initial worktree was clean. The existing Registry, settings, workspace scope,
provider configuration, composition, transaction and migration baseline passed
163 tests. A configured local Provider proxy answered authenticated model discovery
and advertised the configured DeepSeek model; generation is still to be validated.

## Minimum-change implementation sequence

1. Add durable Trigger/Thread subscriptions and bounded full-content readback;
   reuse the existing transaction, event and Worker Inbox mechanisms.
2. Add typed Chain of Recall and private Worker execution directories; expose
   bounded read tools to the Router and Worker while preserving authorization.
3. Add a trusted host delegation mandate for new conversational tasks. Create
   a minimal internal execution contract and select a Worker through the existing
   Model Intelligence Registry/Composer. A mandate never impersonates `local_user`,
   grants external action approval or expands the existing workspace boundary.
   Existing manual plans and authenticated approvals retain their behavior.
4. Connect cold-start semantic filtering, direct follow-ups, timer/file/external
   intake and results to the single Router. Persist intake deduplication and
   processing state so restarts do not create duplicate tasks or lose events.
5. Connect an independent Watchdog and generic workspace association to Core
   startup/shutdown. Recover only replay-safe work; unresolved effects remain
   unresolved and block replay under the existing evidence mechanisms.
6. Test migration/rollback, dedupe/fanout/handback, scoped readback, autonomy
   boundaries, concurrency, restart, supervision and integration. Run bounded
   real Provider scenarios and retain redacted results, actual usage, failed
   observations and explicit limitations. No synthetic result counts as live.

## Acceptance

One user conversation accepts new work while hidden Workers run concurrently.
New work is dispatched without asking the user to manage sessions or allocate
Agents. Follow-up events reach subscribed Workers without Router inference.
Worker results return through the Router. State and object references survive
restart. Watchdog detects and handles crashes/timeouts without replaying unknown
side effects. Cross-project continuity uses recalled references rather than
requiring repeated task explanations. High-risk tool authorization is still
enforced at execution, independent of autonomous task scheduling.

No frontend rewrite, external runtime dependency, cosmetic Manager layer,
deletion of historical evidence, or manual Entire checkpoint is part of this plan.

# FORGE v4 — General-purpose Super-agent

FORGE is a self-built, general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent desktop
application: one persistent Router conversation coordinates hidden, isolated
Workers and continuously receives events.

## Engineering status — 2026-11-16

The backend architecture is being corrected around DeepSeek Super-agent's
persistent Router and independent Workers. The default Core delegates ordinary
conversational tasks automatically, filters environmental events, sends Thread
continuations directly to subscribed Workers, follows typed Chain of Recall
references, and supervises durable execution. Plans, Quests and approval records
are internal infrastructure. The frontend is unchanged in this correction.

Read the [architecture audit and refactor plan](docs/SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[product architecture](docs/PRODUCT_ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[implementation and validation report](docs/SUPERAGENT_IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md)
for the exact implemented behavior, tests, real Provider observations and limits.
Historical Phase 2 evidence remains available below; it does not describe the
new autonomous dispatch path.

See the [current status](docs/PHASE2_STATUS.md), [Phase 2 report](docs/PHASE2_AGENT_INTELLIGENCE_REPORT.md),
[experiments](docs/PHASE2_EXPERIMENTS.md) and [V22 historical boundary](docs/audit/phase2/acceptance-independent-v22-boundary.md).
Historical failures and original evidence remain preserved. The real algorithm
microstudy scored 25/90 task successes; it does not establish general policy gains.
Frontend work is being handled separately; packaging is outside this sprint.

Phase 1 Milestones 1–6 provide the persistence, governance, Registry, DAG, native Workers, tool/evidence and context/budget foundation. Historical M6 verification passed 372 tests; one bounded live continuation succeeded after five retained diagnostic failures. The [M7 backend hardening round](docs/PHASE1_MILESTONE7_BACKEND_HARDENING.md) passed 488 local tests. Desktop Alpha, final native integration and packaging are deferred; these historical backend results do not establish a desktop release.

See [current status](docs/STATUS.md), the [Phase 0 audit report](docs/PHASE0_AUDIT.md), and the report's dependency-ordered development plan. The release references `codex/MASTER_PROMPT.md`, but that file is missing from the supplied archive.

**The user has one persistent conversation.** A persistent Router Agent owns that conversation and coordinates multiple long-running Quests and hidden Worker Sessions. Workers have isolated execution contexts, but they are never presented as separate user conversations.

## Product invariants

1. One persistent user-facing conversation per workspace.
2. One persistent Router identity and resumable state per workspace.
3. Multiple durable Quests can run behind that conversation.
4. Worker Sessions are private execution contexts, not user-facing chats.
5. Worker events are selectively relayed into the single conversation timeline.
6. Model Provider, Model Profile, Role Template, Agent Instance, Quest and Session are separate domain entities.
7. Model Registry uses provider metadata, FORGE benchmark results, online performance and explicit user overrides.
8. Team composition combines reusable role templates with bounded dynamic role synthesis.
9. FORGE owns its Agent Loop, Router, Worker Runtime, Tool Engine, Memory, Governance and Evidence.
10. DeepSeek Super-agent defines the overall architecture; Codex and Claude Code inform Harness design. None is an execution backend.

## What this release contains

- Typed Python domain layer and repository interfaces.
- SQLite persistence with schema versioning and transaction boundaries.
- Persistent `main` conversation and Router identity.
- Quest lifecycle state machine and hidden Worker Session records.
- Durable event log with sequence cursor.
- Model Registry and explainable capability-fit team composition baseline.
- Provider gateway and explicit unconfigured provider; Mock protocol tests are labelled.
- FastAPI API with input validation and consistent error handling.
- React single-conversation UI with background Quest panel.
- Automated tests for persistence, lifecycle, router classification and team composition.
- Architecture, threat model, ADRs, detailed roadmap and Codex execution prompts.

## Important maturity statement

This is an engineering implementation with bounded context recovery, source-bound
recall and evidence-gated execution. A configured Provider is required; Mock
tests and real Provider observations are identified separately. Autonomous
internal plan/team contracts use an auditable host mandate tied to the original
request or admitted Trigger. Manual approvals retain authenticated user authority,
and risky tool actions still require their own authorization. A mandate or
proposal does not prove execution. Worker directories are private execution
contexts, not an OS sandbox. General complex-task correctness remains subject to
recorded acceptance.

## Backend setup

The model-driven Router requires explicit provider configuration. Set the process environment
variables `FORGE_PROVIDER_ID`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_KIND` (for example `openai_compatible`),
`FORGE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`, `FORGE_PROVIDER_CREDENTIAL_REF` (for example
`FORGE_PROVIDER_KEY_EXAMPLE`), `FORGE_ROUTER_MODEL_ID`, and
`FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` (an operator-supplied maximum context window). Put the actual
credential only in the process environment variable named by the credential reference. Set
`FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_TOOLS=true` and `FORGE_PROVIDER_SUPPORTS_JSON_SCHEMA=true` only when
the provider supports them. Without configuration the Core starts but Router message calls fail
explicitly; no keyword or mock provider is selected automatically. The optional `request_id`
in a message request allows safe retry: reuse it only for the same input.
For live calls, register an enabled model with the same provider and model ID and explicitly set
both `tool_calling_support` and `structured_output_support` to supported. Unknown capabilities
are rejected. Values submitted through the model API are recorded as user overrides.

Provider timing, Worker ownership and review/output limits use the process environment:

| Variable | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` | Defaults to `false`: cumulative workspace, Quest, team and Worker token estimates do not stop execution. Usage is still recorded and unsettled calls remain unresolved. Set `true` to opt into cumulative limits and configure `FORGE_MODEL_TOKEN_LIMIT`. Model context/output limits, concurrency, tool permissions, deadlines and review counts still apply. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` | Per-attempt timeout in seconds; finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `30`. A timeout does not prove the upstream operation stopped. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_MAX_RETRIES` | Additional Gateway retries, integer `0`–`3`; defaults to `1`. Each HTTP attempt requires its own budget admission. |
| `FORGE_WORKER_LEASE_SECONDS` | Worker ownership lease, finite and greater than `0`, at most `600`; defaults to `60`. Valid current owners renew between steps, capped by the task deadline. The local call wait is bounded by the current lease; an upstream operation may remain unresolved after that wait ends. |
| `FORGE_REVIEW_MAX_ROUNDS` | Maximum review rounds; integer `1`–`4`, defaults to `2`. The live acceptance harness explicitly selects `3`, matching its scenario cap. This does not reset budgets or change historical runs. |
| `FORGE_PROVIDER_REASONING_EFFORT` | Optional explicit OpenAI-compatible/DeepSeek request setting: `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` or `max`. Unset sends no setting. Configure only for a model that advertises support; Anthropic configuration rejects it. |
| `FORGE_ROUTER_OUTPUT_RESERVE` | Router response-token ceiling and reserved output allowance; integer `1`–`8192`, defaults to `2048`. `FORGE_ROUTER_CONTEXT_LIMIT` must be greater than this value. A registered model's known output limit must also support it. |
# FORGE Super-agent architecture correction

Date: 2026-11-16. Starting commit: `4b220d8`. Frontend is outside this change.

## Architecture decision

FORGE builds its own general-purpose DeepSeek-style Super-agent. Its product is
one continuous Router conversation with independently executing hidden Workers.
Quest, DAG, team contracts, approvals and evidence are internal infrastructure.
The Router dispatches independent tasks; it does not do detailed task execution.
An execution Worker may use a team internally. Codex and Claude Code inform the
execution harness, context and permissions, rather than the overall architecture.

Primary basis: [DeepSeek Harness article](https://x.com/DeepSeekHarness/status/2116857257245987236),
especially sections 2, 3, 5 and 6, and [official prototype](https://github.com/DeepSeek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype)
at `8c32a9dc5d72c033816c6a8110b37f40cf94fba4`.
The article describes more than the public, single-repository DSH plugin implements.
FORGE adopts the two-layer principles, not its GitHub-only deployment or DSH backend.

## Completed differential audit

Detailed source evidence is in [DeepSeek research](SUPERAGENT_DEEPSEEK_RESEARCH.md),
[harness audit](SUPERAGENT_HARNESS_AUDIT.md) and
[validation baseline](SUPERAGENT_VALIDATION_BASELINE.md).

| Concern | Existing foundation | Gap and minimum correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Persistent Router | Stable `main`, Router ID, durable turns, snapshot/CAS, compaction | Add autonomous delegation to the actual Core lifecycle; keep the Router lightweight |
| Isolated Workers | Hidden session, per-run messages, leases and budgets | Add private per-task execution directories; keep approved input and receipt checks |
| Event triggers | Transactional events/Outbox, Inbox, fenced delivery, retries/dead letters | Durable source/Thread/Trigger intake with code admission and semantic cold-start decisions |
| Subscription/pass-through | Worker commands target one Worker | Many-to-many Thread subscriptions, direct follow-up delivery and explicit handback |
| Inline/Spill | Full message archives, exact hashes and bounded source reads | Apply bounded previews plus complete external content references to triggers/recall |
| Chain of Recall | Sourced lexical/semantic recall, archive links | Typed, bounded traversal across Thread, Trigger, Quest, Worker, event, source and project references |
| Persistent state | SQLite migrations and atomic state/event commits | Persist new trigger/subscription/mandate/watchdog state; use existing contracts and recovery |
| Watchdog | Background exception retry and Worker lease recovery | Independent supervision task, persisted health, timeout/task-exit detection, safe recovery |
| Workspaces | One authoritative workspace binding, optional labels | Generic local manifest/directory discovery and task association, independent of GitHub |
| Model intelligence/teams | Capability provenance, speed/cost, bounded composition | Reuse selection for autonomous independent task assignments rather than ask users to pick Agents |

The initial worktree was clean. The existing Registry, settings, workspace scope,
provider configuration, composition, transaction and migration baseline passed
163 tests. A configured local Provider proxy answered authenticated model discovery
and advertised the configured DeepSeek model; generation is still to be validated.

## Minimum-change implementation sequence

1. Add durable Trigger/Thread subscriptions and bounded full-content readback;
   reuse the existing transaction, event and Worker Inbox mechanisms.
2. Add typed Chain of Recall and private Worker execution directories; expose
   bounded read tools to the Router and Worker while preserving authorization.
3. Add a trusted host delegation mandate for new conversational tasks. Create
   a minimal internal execution contract and select a Worker through the existing
   Model Intelligence Registry/Composer. A mandate never impersonates `local_user`,
   grants external action approval or expands the existing workspace boundary.
   Existing manual plans and authenticated approvals retain their behavior.
4. Connect cold-start semantic filtering, direct follow-ups, timer/file/external
   intake and results to the single Router. Persist intake deduplication and
   processing state so restarts do not create duplicate tasks or lose events.
5. Connect an independent Watchdog and generic workspace association to Core
   startup/shutdown. Recover only replay-safe work; unresolved effects remain
   unresolved and block replay under the existing evidence mechanisms.
6. Test migration/rollback, dedupe/fanout/handback, scoped readback, autonomy
   boundaries, concurrency, restart, supervision and integration. Run bounded
   real Provider scenarios and retain redacted results, actual usage, failed
   observations and explicit limitations. No synthetic result counts as live.

## Acceptance

One user conversation accepts new work while hidden Workers run concurrently.
New work is dispatched without asking the user to manage sessions or allocate
Agents. Follow-up events reach subscribed Workers without Router inference.
Worker results return through the Router. State and object references survive
restart. Watchdog detects and handles crashes/timeouts without replaying unknown
side effects. Cross-project continuity uses recalled references rather than
requiring repeated task explanations. High-risk tool authorization is still
enforced at execution, independent of autonomous task scheduling.

No frontend rewrite, external runtime dependency, cosmetic Manager layer,
deletion of historical evidence, or manual Entire checkpoint is part of this plan.

# FORGE Super-agent backend correction

Date: 2026-11-16. Base: `4b220d8bdbd834bbadda53d0baa7756e9c1bb90f`.
The frontend is unchanged. Research preceded implementation; see the
[architecture difference audit and plan](SUPERAGENT_REFACTOR_PLAN.md),
[DeepSeek source research](SUPERAGENT_DEEPSEEK_RESEARCH.md) and
[Harness audit](SUPERAGENT_HARNESS_AUDIT.md).

## Resulting architecture

The normal Core entry point uses the persistent Router as the sole conversational
Agent. A request needing execution receives a source-bound host mandate. Internal
execution contracts reuse the existing graph, team and Registry implementation;
routine task admission does not require a human plan/team approval. The mandate
has its own `router_mandate:<id>` actor and cannot impersonate `local_user`.

| Requirement | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Persistent Router | Existing stable `main` conversation/Router identity, bounded context and CAS; autonomous delegation in the real Core lifecycle; user/event Router inference serialized |
| Isolated Workers | Private messages, run identity, leases, per-run working/temp/output paths; fixed process tools use private cwd and temporary environment; Workers report through Router |
| Event-driven triggers | Durable Source/Thread/Trigger ingress, actor/source Fast Path, semantic batched Slow Path; user messages, existing results, authenticated external ingress, persistent timers and file watches |
| Subscription/pass-through | Many-to-many Thread subscriptions, direct Inbox delivery, ingress dedupe, explicit handback and bounded backpressure reconciliation |
| Inline/Spill | Complete original requests and Trigger payloads retained externally; bounded inline content/previews, exact hashes, paginated source reads |
| Chain of Recall | Scoped typed references between conversations, sources, projects, tasks, Workers, runs, plans, events, evidence, memories, receipts and archives |
| Persistent state | Schema 14 migration within the existing strict migration/rollback mechanism; new state shares SQLite transactions and Outbox/CAS boundaries |
| Watchdog | Durable health, bounded loop recovery, expired-lease reconciliation, environment checks and replay-safe Worker recovery; default CLI parent supervisor with process-tree cleanup |
| Generic workspaces | Manifest/Git/plain-directory detection, persistent project/task association and automatic identification from explicit paths in the immutable request |
| Adaptive composition | Router chooses bounded independent assignments/roles; existing Composer chooses eligible models using capability provenance, context/output limits, speed and cost |
| Local tools | Governed file tools, fixed Python/Git probes and read-only GPU diagnostics; existing separately authorized HTTPS browser/MCP tools retained with their original limits |

No duplicate model manager, new frontend, or external agent execution backend was
introduced. Complex execution planning belongs inside Workers. Autonomous
assignments are coarse, independent contracts with no DAG edges.

Implementation entry points:

- [Core lifecycle and authenticated integration API](../backend/src/forge_api/main.py)
  and [persistent Router](../backend/src/forge_core/router.py).
- [Autonomous delegation](../backend/src/forge_core/superagent_delegation.py),
  [semantic event path](../backend/src/forge_core/superagent_loop.py),
  [subscriptions and fast delivery](../backend/src/forge_core/superagent_events.py),
  and [timer/file sources](../backend/src/forge_core/superagent_sources.py).
- [Recall traversal](../backend/src/forge_core/recall_chain.py),
  [Core source proof](../backend/src/forge_core/worker_core_provenance.py),
  [Worker environment](../backend/src/forge_core/worker_environment.py), and
  [project discovery](../backend/src/forge_core/workspace_discovery.py).
- [Watchdog](../backend/src/forge_core/watchdog.py) and
  [CLI process supervision](../backend/src/forge_api/supervisor.py).
- [Conversational acceptance driver](../backend/scripts/verify_superagent.py)
  and [event/adaptive-team acceptance driver](../backend/scripts/verify_superagent_cold_start.py).

## Authority and delivery boundaries

An internal mandate permits bounded task scheduling and task-local artifact
writes. It grants no external-action approval. Explicit revocations stay revoked;
crash recovery does not silently recreate them. Each execution still passes
existing plan/team authority, workspace scope, action intent/receipt, model-call
ledger and completion evidence checks.

Core context reads have their own trusted, source-bound checkpoint proofs. They
are not fabricated action receipts. Review verifies run/Quest/plan/call identity,
arguments, result hashes, transcripts, actual Trigger delivery and source scope.
Handback commits once at the checkpoint; subsequent review is read-only. A new
Inbox event arriving during final inference prevents result publication until
the Worker has consumed the continuation. Accounting for the draft remains
charged, and step/tool budgets are not reset.

Watchdog recovery never replays an unknown Provider call or tool effect. Exited
loops use bounded backoff and regain restart allowance only after observed
stable operation. Heartbeat storage failures cannot terminate the recovery loop.
On Windows, the CLI supervisor drains the old Job Object process tree before
starting a replacement. Native desktop bootstrap remains compatible.

The Watchdog reports stale heartbeats but does not cancel or duplicate a pending
loop solely because it is stale. The parent supervises process exit, not a live
Core whose event loop is completely hung. This is infrastructure recovery, not
an independent model Session that judges semantic progress or goal drift.

## Verification evidence

The initial infrastructure selection passed **163 tests** before production
changes. The first full regression recorded **2179 passed, 17 failed, 2 skipped**
in [initial regression XML](audit/superagent/backend-regression-initial.xml).
Fourteen failures were reproduced individually with the original source and
tests archived from the base commit, outside the working checkout:
[baseline comparison](audit/superagent/baseline-affected.xml), **209 passed,
14 failed**. They concern previous planner/capacity/output expectations and the
old compact-prompt size assertion. They are retained as baseline failures, not
silenced or presented as passing checks.

The other three failures involved the new automatic lifecycle's old test
expectations and a pseudo-v7 migration fixture containing newer tables. Manual
lifecycle compatibility tests now explicitly use that path; migration fixtures
remove later tables before testing genuine strict historical migration.
Production migrations were not weakened with `IF NOT EXISTS`.

Focused context/state regression:
[121 passed, 2 skipped](audit/superagent/context-state-regression.xml).
Windows skips concern symlink creation privileges. Further final test and real
Provider results are recorded below when completed; intermediate selections
overlap and are not added together as a suite total.

A later complete backend run recorded **2251 passed, 14 failed, 2 skipped** in
[regression XML](audit/superagent/backend-regression-final.xml). Its failures are
exactly the fourteen reproduced baseline failures. The final Router response and
late-attachment corrections are additionally checked in focused tests; they were
motivated by the real diagnostics described below.

The first real Provider diagnostic, `20261115T183233Z-cf6da7`, failed. Two hidden
Workers executed real file tools, two follow-ups passed through without Router
Trigger inference, and all **25 calls / 110935 charged tokens** settled. A late
continuation raced final publication; another Worker successfully read its
Trigger but review did not yet recognize the new Core proof. The
[original redacted diagnosis](audit/superagent/20261115T183233Z-cf6da7-diagnostic.json)
is retained. These failures drove the final-boundary and provenance fixes.

The next conversational diagnostic, `20261115T190232Z-065808`, exhausted its
unchanged 32-call ceiling. One Worker passed independent review; the second user
turn retried its Router snapshot twice while the first task advanced. The driver
waited for both HTTP turns before injecting continuations and missed the first
Worker's execution window. It stopped with two reserved calls; that workspace is
retained and is not replayed. This led to scoped independent-task snapshot checks,
deterministic filtering of routine internal progress, and concurrent probe
submission/observation.

The cold-start diagnostic, `20261115T190431Z-cold-1f2fe2`, completed two independent
Workers and their reviews, verified both files, admitted a timer task, ignored
file noise and traversed Recall. Its report's intermediate checks all passed,
but another notice began between the settled check and shutdown. The final
ledger had one reserved call, so the published `passed` status is superseded by
the accompanying diagnostic and is **not final acceptance**. The probe now gates
final status on the post-stop ledger and waits for settled notification work.
Original reports are preserved; no failed or uncertain call is replayed.

Final responsiveness corrections keep new independent task admission stable
while unrelated Workers change runtime status. Conversation state, messages,
models, constraints, archive head, original task identities, selected recall and
consulted source checks remain fenced; existing-task intents retain the strict
snapshot check. Autonomous routine progress and nonterminal internal status facts
are acknowledged without model calls. Results, blockers, failures, help and
action approvals retain semantic handling.

An event arriving after Worker finalization cannot be attached to a task with
no accepting Worker. Router context exposes recipient availability, and the
transaction rechecks it. Invalid attachment rolls back the entire batch and
leaves the Trigger pending for retry or a new continuation dispatch. This covers
the separate gap between final publication and review completion.

Completed-task status queries now retain a natural Router recap when every
selected task is Core-completed and the current plan has succeeded Worker/node
deliveries. The bounded source summaries and their payload hashes participate
in snapshot validation; the answer carries task/event references. Manual,
unfinished, mixed-state or unsourced cases retain exact Core status facts.
The final Router compatibility and mutation selection passed **153 tests**.

Archive Recall now verifies complete previous-archive dependencies through the
existing ContextService verifier, including original source/index/scope/hashes,
cycles and link hashes. Revoking an original user message, internal Worker
message or previous archive blocks dependent recall, including legacy inherited
sources. The combined new archive, Recall and Core proof selection passed
**43 tests**. The final event, backpressure, proof, supervisor, Watchdog, project
and acceptance-driver selection passed **94 tests, 1 skipped**. These overlapping
selections are not a replacement for the complete regression result.

Real acceptance uses authenticated HTTP against isolated Core processes, the
configured `deepseek-v4.1-flash` local proxy, actual file/readback receipts and
durable model usage. Credentials come from process environment only, and are not
written to source or reports. Each driver is bounded to 32 calls, 500000 tokens
and 900 seconds. The proxy-reported upstream model identity is not independently
verified. Scripted protocol tests never count as real Provider evidence.

## Operating limits

- Private Worker directories are not an OS sandbox. Process isolation and tool
  authorization do not isolate an attacker with the same OS account.
- Automatic delegation currently uses a fixed local tool allowlist. Terminal
  inspection is a fixed Python-version probe; Python compilation and pure-function
  AST tests do not provide arbitrary shell, pytest, package installation or
  unrestricted program execution. Git support here is status inspection.
- The retained browser tool is allowlisted HTTPS GET, without rendering or
  interactive browsing. MCP is preconfigured HTTPS JSON-RPC `tools/call`, without
  general stdio/SSE discovery or session management. Both retain independent
  high-risk action authorization and are outside the autonomous default allowlist.
  The final live scenarios exercise file tools, not browser or MCP execution.
- Project discovery establishes identity and Recall continuity. It does not
  expand execution outside the configured workspace or grant project writes.
  Multiple explicit roots retain the neutral storage association.
- Autonomous dispatch allows at most four independent assignments; actual
  concurrency also respects the configured Core and Provider limits.
  Workers plan steps inside their own model loop; autonomous nested-team spawning
  is not implemented. Real acceptance uses one configured model for multiple
  roles and operator-supplied capability priors, not a capability benchmark or
  evidence of optimal selection across different models.
- Host contract allocation bounds are enforced. Cumulative token use is recorded,
  with stopping controlled by `FORGE_ENFORCE_TOKEN_BUDGETS` (default `false`).
  The acceptance drivers explicitly enable their fixed cumulative budgets.
- Timers and file watches are registered by authenticated local host APIs and
  polled by Core. Natural-language creation of schedules/watches is not exposed
  as a Router/Worker tool. External ingress trusts the authenticated local adapter;
  no public webhook server, OAuth/signature adapters or built-in messaging
  connectors are added.
- Automatic whole-Core process restart applies to the default CLI launcher.
  Native `--desktop-host` and direct uvicorn execution do not gain that parent
  supervisor. A running but fully hung process is not automatically restarted.
- Complete Trigger ingress is bounded to 4 MiB; watched files to 1 MiB. Readback
  pages and Recall traversal are bounded, with explicit continuation references.
- GPU support is read-only status through fixed `nvidia-smi` arguments. GPU
  compute scheduling and OS/container security sandboxes are not implemented.
- Tool network access retains operator allowlists and independent action
  authorization. Scheduling a task cannot authorize an external side effect.
- Bounded real scenarios establish observed integration behavior. They do not
  establish arbitrary-task success, indefinite unattended operation or a
  packaged desktop release. The fourteen reproduced historical test failures
  remain visible technical debt.
